facts.text: In the Indian national movement the period from 1920 to 1947 is known as the 'Gandhian era'.
facts.quote: In the Indian national movement the period from 1920 to 1947 is known as the 'Gandhian era'.

facts.text: After the death of Lokmanya Tilak in 1920, the reins of the national movement went into the hands of Mahatma Gandhi.
facts.quote: After the death of Lokmanya Tilak in 1920, the reigns of national movement went into the hands of Mahatma Gandhi.

facts.text: Gandhi gave a new direction to the freedom movement with the principles of Truth, Non violence and Satyagraha.
facts.quote: He gave a new direction to the freedom movement with the principles of Truth, Non violence and Satyagraha.

facts.text: Mahatma Gandhi went to South Africa, a British colony, for some legal work in 1893.
facts.quote: Mahatma Gandhi went to South Africa for some legal work in 1893. South Africa was a colony of the British.

facts.text: In 1906 the Government in South Africa made it compulsory for the blacks to carry an identity card; Gandhiji followed the path of Satyagraha against the injustice.
facts.quote: In 1906, the Government declared that the it was compulsory for the blacks to carry an identity card and their freedom was restricted as well. Gandhiji followed the path of Satyagraha against the injustice

facts.text: On 9th January 1915 Gandhiji returned to India from South Africa and, as suggested by Gopal Krishna Gokhale, made a tour of the entire nation.
facts.quote: On 9th January 1915, Gandhiji returned to India from South Africa. As suggested by Gopal Krishna Gokhale, he made a tour of the entire nation.

facts.text: Gandhiji took up the vow of service to the nation and stayed at the Sabarmati Ashram in Ahmedabad.
facts.quote: He took up the vow of service to the nation. He stayed at the Sabarmati Ashram in Ahmedabad.

facts.text: Satyagraha means insistence of truth; a person following satyagraha should never use violence and untruth means.
facts.quote: Satyagraha means insistence of truth. ... A person following satyagraha should never use violence and untruth means, was the teachings of Gandhiji.

facts.text: Gandhiji's path of Satyagraha made an impact on Martin Luther King in America and on Nelson Mandela in South Africa.
facts.quote: Gandhiji's path of Satyagraha made on impact on Martin Luther King who was struggling for the rights of the Blacks in America, as well as on Nelson Mandela in South Africa.

facts.text: The farmers of Champaran in Bihar were forced to cultivate indigo; Gandhiji went to Champaran in 1917 and his first war of independence in India became successful.
facts.quote: In Bihar, the farmers of Champaran region were forced to cultivate indigo. ... Gandhiji went to Champaran in 1917. ... Gandhiji's first war of independence in India became successful and the farmers were given justice.

facts.text: In Kheda district, Gujarat, land tax was forcibly collected though crops failed; the farmers began the movement for scrapping of tax in 1918 and the Government suspended the tax.
facts.quote: Due to constant famines in Kheda district, Gujrat, the crop had failed. Still land tax was forcibly collected by the Government. ... The farmers began the movement for scraping of tax at Kheda in 1918. ... the Government suspended the tax.

facts.text: At Ahmedabad the mill owners rejected the mill workers' demand for a rise in salary; on Gandhiji's advice the workers went on hunger strike and their salary was increased.
facts.quote: Mill workers demanded for rise in salary. But the mill owners rejected this demand. As per Gandhiji's advice, the workers went on hunger strike. Finally, the mill owners had to back off and the salary of workers was increased.

facts.text: A Committee was appointed under Sir Sydney Rowlatt; on its recommendations a new law, the 'Rowlatt Act', was passed on 17 March 1919.
facts.quote: a Committee was appointed under Sir Sydney Rowlatt. According to recommendations of this committee a new law was passed ... on 17 March 1919. This law came to be known as 'Rowlatt Act'.

facts.text: The Rowlatt Act allowed arrest without any warrant and imprisonment without any trial, and appeal was prohibited; Indians called it the 'Black Act'.
facts.quote: This Act gave the right to the government to arrest anybody without any warrant or imprison without any trial. Appeal was prohibited against the punishment given through this act. The Indians called this act as 'Black Act'

facts.text: On 6th April 1919 Gandhiji appealed to the Indians to follow Hartal all over India against the Rowlatt Act.
facts.quote: On 6th April 1919, he appealed to the Indians to follow Hartal all over India against the Act.

facts.text: Amritsar in Punjab became the main centre of the movement; Gandhiji was prohibited from entering Punjab, General Dyer banned public meetings in Amritsar, and Dr.Satyapal and Dr.Kitchelu were arrested.
facts.quote: Amritsar became the main centre of this movement. ... Gandhiji was prohibited from entering the province of Punjab. General Dyer issued orders of ban on public meetings in Amritsar. Important leaders like Dr.Satyapal and Dr.Kitchelu were arrested for their involvement in Amritsar Hartal case.

facts.text: On 13th April 1919, a Baisakhi day, people assembled at Jallianwala Baug in Amritsar; the place had only one small gate, which General Dyer closed before ordering his soldiers to fire.
facts.quote: on 13th April 1919, on a Baisakhi day, the people of Amritsar assembled at a place named Jallianwala Baug. ... had only one small gate. General Dyer positioned his army and closed down the only gate. ... he ordered his soldiers to fire.

facts.text: At Jallianwala Baug 1660 rounds were fired until the ammunition was over, and about 400 people were killed.
facts.quote: 1660 rounds, had been fired. The army continued firing until the ammunition was over. In this massacre about 400 people including men and women were killed.

facts.text: After the firing a curfew was announced, and military law was enforced in entire Punjab.
facts.quote: After firing curfew was announced ... In entire Punjab, military law was enforced and many were sent to jail by the government.

facts.text: General Michael O'Dwyer, Governor of Punjab, was responsible for the massacre.
facts.quote: General Michael O'Dwyer, Governor of Punjab, was responsible for this massacre.

facts.text: As a protest against the massacre, Rabindranath Tagore gave away the title of 'Sir' bestowed on him by the British Government.
facts.quote: As a protest against this massacre, Rabindranath Tagore gave away the title of 'Sir' bestowed on him by the British Government.

facts.text: Indians demanded an enquiry into the massacre, so the British government appointed the Hunter Commission.
facts.quote: Later Indians demanded for enquiry of this massacre, hence the British government appointed the Hunter Commission.

facts.text: Muslims regarded the ruler of Turkey as their religious leader; England broke its assurance about the Khalifa's empire, and the movement of Indian Muslims to support the Khalifa was called the 'Khilafat Movement'.
facts.quote: Muslims all over the world regarded the ruler of Turkey as their religious leader. During the first world war Turkey fought against the British. ... The movement started by Indian Muslims to support the Khalifa was called 'Khilafat Movement'.

facts.text: Gandhiji supported the Khilafat Movement; the Khilafat Committee accepted his proposal of non-co-operation, and Hindu-Muslim unity was seen especially during this period.
facts.quote: Therefore Gandhiji supported the Khilafat Movement. The Khilafat Committee accepted Gandhiji's proposal of following non-co-operation to the government. Hindu-Muslim unity was seen especially during this period.

facts.text: The concept of Non-co-operation: the British government in India depends only on the co-operation of the Indians, so complete non-co-operation would make it collapse.
facts.quote: the British government in India is dependent only on the co-operation of the Indians. If the Indians adopted complete non-co-operation then the British government will completely collapse.

facts.text: In 1920 the Indian National Congress session was held at Nagpur, where the resolution of Non-co-operation put forth by Chittaranjan Das was accepted.
facts.quote: In 1920, the Indian National Congress session was held at Nagpur. The resolution of Non-co-operation movement put forth by Chittaranjan Das was accepted.

facts.text: The Nagpur resolution framed a programme to boycott Government offices, courts, foreign goods, Government schools and colleges.
facts.quote: a programme was framed to boycott Government offices, courts, foreign goods, Government schools and colleges.

facts.text: Eminent lawyers like Motilal Nehru and Chittaranjan Das gave up their practice; national schools, colleges and universities were set up and foreign clothes were burnt, so their import decreased.
facts.quote: many eminent lawyers like Motilal Nehru, Chittaranjan Das etc. boycotted the court by giving up their practice. ... Many National schools, colleges and universities were established. ... boycott and bonfire of foreign clothes. Due to this the import of foreign clothes decreased.

facts.text: In 1921, during the visit of the Prince of Wales, he was welcomed with a hartal: lonely roads and closed shops.
facts.quote: In 1921, during the visit of Prince of Wales, he was welcomed by organising hartal. Lonely roads and closed shops welcomed the Prince.

facts.text: The movement spread from the planters in Assam to rail workers in Bengal.
facts.quote: The movement spread from the planters in Assam to rail workers in Bengal.

facts.text: In February 1922 the police fired on a peaceful procession at Chauri Chaura in Gorakhpur district of Uttar Pradesh; angry people set fire to the police station and one officer and 22 policemen were killed.
facts.quote: In February 1922, the Police opened fire on a peaceful procession at Chauri Chaura in Gorakhpur district of Uttar Pradesh. The people were angry and set fire to the police station in which along with one officer, 22 policemen were killed.

facts.text: Hurt by the Chauri Chaura incident, Gandhiji suspended the Non-co-operation Movement on 12 February 1922.
facts.quote: Due to this incident, Gandhiji was hurt. On 12 February 1922, Gandhiji suspended the Non-co-operation Movement.

facts.text: Do you know: during the Non-co-operation Movement, farmers of Mulshi Taluka in Pune district launched satyagraha led by Senapati Pandurang Mahadev Bapat, who was punished with six years of imprisonment.
facts.quote: During the non-co-operation movement, the farmers of Mulshi Taluka in Pune district launched satyagraha against the government. Senapati Pandurang Mahadev Bapat led the Mulshi satyagraha, for which he was punished with six years of imprisonment.

facts.text: Gandhiji was arrested in March 1922 for writing three anti-national articles in 'Young India'; a special court at Ahmedabad sentenced him to six years of imprisonment.
facts.quote: Gandhiji was arrested in March 1922 for writing three anti-national articles in 'Young India'. Special court was set up at Ahmedabad and Gandhiji was sentenced six years of imprisonment.

facts.text: Along with the non-co-operation movement, Gandhiji took up constructive programmes such as Swadeshi, Hindu-Muslim unity, prohibition of alcohol, removal of untouchability, Khadi and national education; he was later released from jail on grounds of ill health.
facts.quote: Later, on grounds of ill health, Gandhiji was released from the jail. Gandhiji ... took up constructive programmes which mainly included spread of Swadeshi, Hindu-Muslim unity, prohibition of alchohol, removal of untouchability, popularise use of Khadi, national education etc.

facts.text: Chittaranjan Das and Motilal Nehru put up the idea of contesting elections and obstructing the British government; the Swaraj Party was established in 1922.
facts.quote: The members of Indian National Congress such as Chittaranjan Das, Motilal Nehru put up the idea of contesting elections and obstructing the work of the British government. In 1922, the Swaraj Party was established.

facts.text: In 1923 many Swaraj Party members were elected to the Central Legislative Assembly and Provincial Legislative Council, mainly Motilal Nehru, Madan Mohan Malviya, Lala Lajpat Rai and N.C.Kelkar.
facts.quote: In 1923, many members of Swaraj Party were elected in the Central Legislative Assembly and Provincial Legislative Council, mainly including Motilal Nehru, Madan Mohan Malviya, Lala Lajpat Rai and N.C.Kelkar.

facts.text: The Swaraj Party demanded Responsible Government for India, and moved resolutions for the release of political leaders and to call the Round Table Conference; the government rejected most of them.
facts.quote: They demanded that Responsible Government should be given to India in future. They made a resolution ... for the release of political leaders from prison, to call for the Round Table Conference. The government rejected most of the resolutions.

facts.text: The reforms of the Montague Chelmsford Act of 1919 were unsatisfactory; the British appointed a commission under Sir John Simon with no Indian member, so the Congress decided to boycott it.
facts.quote: The reforms introduced by the Montague Chelmsford Act of 1919 were unsatisfactory. ... the British appointed a commission under the chairmanship of Sir John Simon. In this commission, none of the Indian member was included. Hence the Congress decided to boycott the commission.

facts.text: In 1928 the Simon Commission arrived in India; wherever it travelled people shouted 'Simon Go Back'.
facts.quote: In 1928, the commission arrived in India. Wherever it travelled, the people made demonstrations against them, by shouting the slogans like 'Simon Go Back'.

facts.text: At Lahore, Lala Lajpat Rai led the demonstration against the Simon Commission; police officer Saunders attacked him with a lathi; Lalaji said every blow would prove a nail in the coffin of the British Empire, and died within a few days.
facts.quote: At Lahore, Lala Lajpat Rai was leading the demonstration against the Simon Commission. ... Saunders, a police officer, attacked Lalaji with a lathi. ... "Every blow on my body will prove a nail in the coffin of the British Empire". Within few days of the attack Lalaji died.

facts.text: Berkenhead, Secretary of State of India, criticised that Indian leaders cannot draft a unanimously accepted constitution; an all party Committee was formed with Pandit Motilal Nehru as Chairman.
facts.quote: Berkenhead, Secretary of State of India, criticised that the Indian leaders cannot draft a unanimously accepted constitution. This challenge was accepted and an all party Committee was formed. Pandit Motilal Nehru was the Chairman of this Committee.

facts.text: The 'Nehru Report' proposed self government in the colonies of India, Adult Franchise and linguistic division of provinces.
facts.quote: To establish self government in the colonies of India, implement Adult Franchise system, linguistic division of provinces such proposals were put up in this report. This report was known as 'Nehru Report'.

facts.text: By the end of 1929 it was indicated that the civil disobedience movement would start if the Nehru report was not accepted; in December 1929 the Lahore session was presided by Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru.
facts.quote: By the end of 1929, an indication was given that if the Nehru report is not accepted by the government then the civil disobedience movement will be started. On this background, in December 1929, the Lahore session presided by Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru became memorable in history.

facts.text: Young leaders like Pandit Nehru and Subhash Chandra Bose demanded complete independence (poorna swaraj); the Lahore session passed this resolution and Congress gave up the objective of dominion status.
facts.quote: Young leaders like Pandit Nehru and Subhash Chandra Bose were demanding complete independence. i.e. poorna swaraj. ... in the Lahore session of Indian National Congress, resolution of attainment of complete independence was passed. Through this resolution Indian national Congress gave up the objective of dominion status.

facts.text: On 31st December 1929 Pandit Nehru unfurled the tri colour flag, and a resolution declared that 26 January be celebrated as Independence Day.
facts.quote: On 31st December 1929, Pandit Nehru unfurled the tri colour flag and a resolution was passed in which 26 January was declared to be celebrated as Independence Day.

facts.text: On 26 January 1930 people all over the country took a pledge to carry out the freedom movement with non violent means for the independence of India.
facts.quote: On 26 January 1930, people all over the country took pledge for carrying out the freedom movement with non violent means for attainment of independence of India.
